Record date: 2129-12-12
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 12/12/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Worsening shortness of breath, persistent cough, and increased fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for his follow-up appointment one week after his last visit. He reports a deterioration in his respiratory status, noting that his shortness of breath has intensified, particularly during minimal exertion. His cough persists, with occasional production of yellow sputum, which he describes as having increased in volume. Mr. Fairfax expresses concern regarding his overall fatigue, which has become more pronounced, leading to difficulty in performing daily activities. He denies any fever, chills, or chest pain but mentions that his night sweats have returned intermittently.
Despite adherence to the prescribed medication regimen, including Azithromycin and Prednisone, Mr. Fairfax feels that his symptoms have not improved as expected. He has continued to use his nebulizer every 6 hours, but reports that his wheezing has not significantly decreased.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + significant fatigue, - weight loss, - fever, - chills, + night sweats. Pulmonary - + persistent productive cough with yellow sputum, + increased wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 130/76 mmHg - Heart Rate: 80 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 30 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 84% on room air.
General: The patient appears fatigued and is in moderate respiratory distress.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Moderate wheezing on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with significant rhonchi present.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with worsening respiratory status despite treatment; persistent cough and increased shortness of breath necessitate reevaluation of therapy. 2. Possible underlying infection or inadequate response to current medications; sputum characteristics warrant further investigation. 3. Congestive heart failure remains stable; no signs of fluid overload or exacerbation.
PLAN
1. Order a chest X-ray to evaluate for possible pneumonia or other complications contributing to Mr. Fairfax's respiratory decline. 2. Continue Azithromycin 500 mg daily to complete the course; consider adding a course of oral Levofloxacin if there is suspicion of a bacterial superinfection based on sputum analysis. 3. Maintain oral Prednisone 20 mg daily for one more week to manage inflammation; evaluate the need for a higher dose if no improvement is noted. 4. Increase Salmeterol to 200 mcg twice daily and consider adding a short-acting beta-agonist (SABA) for immediate relief of acute symptoms. 5. Schedule a follow-up appointment in 3 days to reassess clinical status and response to the adjusted treatment plan; monitor for any signs of exacerbation or hospitalization. 6. Educate Mr. Fairfax on the importance of utilizing his nebulizer more frequently during this exacerbation and to recognize signs of potential worsening, such as increased sputum production or changes in color.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was discharged home with a revised medication regimen, including continuation of Azithromycin, Prednisone, and an increased dose of Salmeterol. He was advised to undergo a chest X-ray and to return for follow-up in 3 days for further evaluation. He was instructed to monitor his symptoms closely and to seek immediate medical attention if his condition deteriorates.
